instruction: use BOTH!!! arms to lift the pot

calls.reason: Begin a small symmetric joint movement to observe both arms' approach direction.
Extend both arms further into the visible workspace with open grippers.
Lower the shoulder angle while bending both elbows to bring the grippers toward the table.
Change elbow direction to orient both grippers toward the tabletop.
Turn both arms inward and continue the elbow movement while keeping both grippers open.
Reverse the base turns based on camera motion and advance both shoulders with a positive elbow bend.
Bring the open grippers closer to the handle locations while preserving the observed wrist pitch.
Adjust the wrist pitch above the handles and inspect the resulting gripper approach.
Pitch both wrists downward toward the pot handles using the observed wrist direction.
Test the fourth-joint wrist orientation while maintaining the arm position above the pot.
Rotate the fourth joints downward to establish a top-down approach to both handles.
Advance both open grippers toward their respective handles with the wrists directed downward.
Correct the lateral alignment and move the forearms toward the handle height.
Extend the forearms toward the handles while maintaining the downward gripper orientation.
Increase fingertip reach toward the handles by reducing the downward wrist angle.
Spread the grippers back toward the handle bars and lower their shared approach height.
Lower both arms using the observed shoulder response and widen the approach to the two outer handles.
Lower each gripper toward its handle and correct the lateral offset seen in the wrist views.
Move both open grippers inward to center the outer handle bars between the fingers.
Correct the wrist-camera centering and extend the shoulder approach while compensating wrist pitch.
Advance the left gripper toward its handle and bring the right handle toward the middle of its wrist view.
Close both grippers around the handle bars now positioned near the finger openings.
Make a small coordinated lift with both grippers closed and inspect whether the pot rises.
The pot stayed on the table; reopen both grippers and lower the fingertip approach toward the handle bars.
Lower the open fingers another small increment and allow the grippers to finish opening before checking alignment.
Advance the lowered grippers toward the bars while retaining their current approach angle.
Make a small lateral correction so the visible handle segments align with the closing finger paths.
Close both grippers at the adjusted handle positions and allow the grip command to settle.
Test a small lift after the visible handle contact, holding both gripper commands steady.
Reopen and align the handles with the observed closed-finger meeting point in each wrist camera.
Adjust the two arms independently to bring the handle bars to the finger-tip depth in both wrist views.
Center the shifted handle bars on the observed grasp locations in the wrist images.
Close both grippers with each handle aligned at the finger meeting point.
Finish closing both grippers around the bars before another coordinated lift.
Lift both closed grippers a small distance while checking for sustained handle attachment.
Reposition above the rotated handles with open grippers and a steeper downward approach.
Move toward the far left handle and nearer right handle while preserving the steeper approach angle.
Advance the left fingertips toward the far handle and move the right handle into its gripper's closing path.
Bring the far handle into the left wrist view and shift the near handle toward the right finger meeting point.
Raise the right gripper clear of the handle before correcting its lateral position.
Continue lifting the open right gripper slightly to separate it from the pot before realignment.
Raise the right forearm while maintaining wrist pitch to gain clearance above the pot.
Shift the raised right gripper laterally so its closing center approaches the near handle bar.
Separate the arms after the measured joint targets diverged, creating clearance for right-handle alignment.
Center the right handle at the closed-finger location and lower the gripper toward its middle.
Lower and center the right gripper on the middle of the near handle bar.
Correct the right-hand alignment from the observed image shift while preserving the downward wrist orientation.
Move the right handle's middle toward the closed-finger center with a small lateral and height correction.
Close the right gripper on the bar centered between its finger tips while leaving the left gripper open.
Apply a small right-forearm lift to check that the handle is retained before bringing in the left arm.
The right handle was not retained; reopen and advance the fingers farther onto the bar at a slightly lower height.
Recenter the handle after advancing the right gripper deeper into the approach.
Raise the right forearm slightly to bring the full handle bar into the grasp region of the wrist view.
Align the right bar's middle with the closed-finger center at the revised approach depth.
Finish the right bar-centering adjustment before closing.
Move the right gripper closer along the handle approach; image alignment alone has not yet produced contact at the finger tips.
Recenter the enlarged right handle after moving closer to it.
Advance closer to the right handle while compensating the lateral shift caused by the approach.
Aim the right fingertips at the enlarged bar by adjusting wrist pitch and a small lateral offset.
Refine the right wrist angle so the handle middle lies between the fingertips at the current depth.
Close the right gripper on the nearby centered handle bar.
Check right-handle retention with a short forearm lift before adding the left grip.
Continue the retention check over a small additional distance while watching the pot and handle.
Reopen and approach the right bar more deeply; the previous lift showed that it was still beyond the fingertips.
Pitch the right fingers toward the nearby handle while keeping the arm's deeper approach position.
Center the nearby right handle across the gripper before closing at the revised depth.
Close the right gripper with the bar at fingertip depth and refine the wrist angle during closure.
Reopen and rotate the right fingers to close more nearly across the bar, correcting for the pot's small shift.
Close the right fingers across the vertically aligned handle bar in the wrist view.
Test retention with the right fingers now oriented across the handle bar.
Advance the open right fingers a little farther onto the handle while keeping their cross-bar orientation.
Aim the deeper right-hand approach back onto the handle bar using a small wrist-pitch change.
Adjust the right wrist upward to bring the handle back into view at the current close approach.
Close across the visible right bar after the close-range wrist-angle correction.
Make a final small right-bar centering correction with the fingers open.
Close the right gripper with the bar centered between the visible finger tips.
Check whether the right bar remains fixed in the fingers during a small forearm lift.
Bring the left gripper toward the far handle while returning the right fingers to their handle approach.
Bring the left fingertips closer to the far handle and aim the open fingers toward its bar.
Advance the left shoulder with wrist compensation to measure how the far handle approaches the fingers.
Adjust the left forearm to bring the far bar lower in the wrist view without changing the approach pitch.
Advance the left approach toward the far bar and compensate its image offset with shoulder, elbow, and base adjustments.
Rotate the left gripper so its fingers close across the far handle bar.
Bring the rotated left handle bar into the left gripper's closing region.
Close the left gripper on the far handle while holding the right gripper closed on the near side.
Lift both forearms together with both grippers closed and check whether the pot rises with them.
Advance both open fingertips toward the handle bars with a shallower wrist approach after the missed lift.
Hold the open grippers briefly and inspect the pot after the visible contact changed its orientation.
Clear the pot and move both arms back toward the now left-right handle positions.
Hold position and observe where the pot settles after leaving the camera view during the arm motion.
Look downward with both wrist cameras to locate the pot after it left the head-camera view.
Survey the outer sides of the tabletop with open grippers to search for the displaced pot.
Raise the wrist-camera viewpoints for a wider survey of the tabletop and surrounding area.
Sweep both raised wrist views outward to search beyond the central tabletop.
Sweep the raised wrist cameras in the opposite direction to inspect the remaining table edges.
Inspect farther outside both sides of the work area for the displaced pot.
Search the forward and opposite edges of the work area using both raised wrist cameras.
Inspect behind the arm bases and the rear table edges for the missing pot.
Sweep the rear outside sectors around both bases to look for the displaced pot.
Lower the camera viewpoints outside the table to inspect floor areas hidden by the tabletop.
Inspect low beside both bases for a pot that may have fallen outside the table.
Extend the cameras down outside the table for a closer view of the surrounding floor.
Survey farther away from the table at a shallower camera angle while continuing the pot search.
